source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten references. Three-epoch reasoning was checked against Fraser; performance and boundedness limitations against Hart, Brown, and Kim-Brown-Singh; current guarded-pointer/deferred-destruction behavior against Crossbeam; and related safe-reclamation, RCU/QSBR, and production APIs against the C++ draft, perfbook, liburcu, and Concurrency Kit. Nine sources resolved directly; ACM denied automated retrieval for Brown's publisher page, so it supports bibliographic and scoped abstract-level attribution only, not quotations or inaccessible details.

evidence: Definitions and Notation consistently defines G, local L_i, active_i, retirement bags B_e, quiescent states Q_i, retire/eligible predicates, rate lambda, size s, duration D, and epoch lag.
The chapter separates reachability, retirement, grace-period eligibility, deferred callback scheduling, destruction, reuse, and reclamation debt.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Checked state transitions, modular-epoch qualifiers, units, approximation notation, and EBR/QSBR/RCU terminology boundaries.

evidence: Recomputed 50,000 nodes/s times 60 s as 3,000,000 nodes and times 128 bytes as 384,000,000 bytes before overhead.
artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-056/report.json records advance 0-to-1, blocked advance while reader remains epoch 0, debt A/B, advances to 2/3, reclamation A then B, and empty remainder.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The debt estimate is conditional and excludes bursts, baseline bags, allocator metadata, callback state, and unmanaged objects.

evidence: For the stated three-bag rule, an epoch-e reader may survive the first advance but must quiesce/refresh before the second; after unlink it cannot reacquire the e-retired object on repin.
The debt relation lambda*D objects and lambda*D*s bytes follows from steady retirement during one blocking interval and becomes unbounded when D has no finite bound.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Two-advance eligibility is deliberately scoped to complete registration, exact advancement/order rules, no pointer escape, exact retirement, and wrap-safe comparison.

evidence: Reviewed entry-before-load, one/two advances, quiescence, repin, nested guards, guard escape, exact wrap, missed/incoherent participant records, and conservative delayed callbacks.

Reviewed stalled/crashed participants, async/blocking regions, thread migration/exit, local bag loss, double retirement, mutable payloads, callback affinity/failure, cancellation, allocation exhaustion, mixed domains, restart, shutdown, and high-stakes use.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary analysis covers lifetime, ordering, progress, debt, registration, language integration, resources, callbacks, lifecycle, operations, and safety.

evidence: Pin publication precedes protected acquisition; all guarded pointers die before quiescence; nesting leaves active state until outer exit; unlink precedes one retirement.

Advancement includes every registered active participant; old bags reclaim only after required quiescent passage; exit transfers local debt; shutdown drains guards, bags, and callbacks before collector destruction.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked invariants across register, pin, load, traverse, nest, unlink, retire, flush, scan, advance, unpin, callback, cancel, exit, close, restart, and destroy.

evidence: The safety argument connects pre-unlink acquisition, guarded lifetime, complete advancement observations, quiescent passage, and inability to reacquire an unreachable node.
The stalled-participant counterargument correctly shows why coarse metadata prevents safe selective reclamation and why logical completions do not imply reclamation liveness or bounded memory.
proof_review.notes: This is a scoped internal proof review, not mechanized source refinement, weak-memory proof, allocator/callback liveness proof, or safety certification.

evidence: Three-bag/two-advance reasoning and lambda-D debt are explicitly labeled common-model proof sketch and estimate, not universal implementation theorems.
Lifetime safety, payload synchronization, linearizability, ABA resistance, logical lock-freedom, collector progress, debt boundedness, callback promptness, and availability remain separate.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter distinguishes abstract mechanism, exact library contract, engineering policy, empirical evidence, and named human safety review.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-056 passed the deterministic advancement/debt model with recorded interpreter version, exact stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit code.

The chapter requires schedule barriers, poisoned reuse, sanitizer/model/weak-memory tests, target inspection, pause/cancel/exit/restart/shutdown stress, callback faults, and debt/guard/advance telemetry.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The sequential model proves no concurrent EBR implementation, source lifetime, weak-memory ordering, wrap safety, exact-once integration, collector progress, memory bound, callback execution, performance, or deployment safety.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed object/participant state, entry ordering, retirement, three-epoch grace periods, EBR versus QSBR/RCU, debt, ordering/wrap, progress, async/failure, domain shutdown, verification, observability, and alternatives.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed nonescaping guards, nesting, thread affinity, batching/local bags, byte-based admission, long-pin policy, exact retire ownership, deferred callback context, failure containment, domain consistency, metrics/alerts, restart isolation, and quiescent drain.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet foregrounds cheap coarse protection versus collective quiescence; exposition derives two-advance reasoning and its limits; the debt model is reproducible; ten examples are distinct; and five exercises progress from entry order to industrial-robot transfer with complete matching answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external concurrency-theory, formal-methods, C++/Rust, compiler, architecture, allocator, EBR/RCU/QSBR, operating-system, async-runtime, real-time, railway, robotics, regulatory, operational, or safety review is claimed. The chapter and model establish neither source safety nor data-structure linearizability, lifetime correctness, ABA prevention, wrap correctness, reclamation/callback liveness, lock-free progress, bounded debt, performance, or deployment safety.
